$comment: Case 1's caller items (docs/fixture-money.md, Caller items on the preview seed): Priya's agent explains each receiving feature's differing calls and classifies every one of them as intended with the reason under calls; that feature's agent reviews the explanation. 'kinds' gives the words for the features scale.py generates, by their kind, with {title} filled in (scale.caller_words).

explanations.cohort-ltv: ShopperMap.resolve() now links the identities a login or a shared verified email ties together, one account per device. Your retention test sees a later login lower a published day's count. Penguin's update copies accounts/shoppers.py and analytics/activity.py into your fork. Rule count-by-cutover rewrites your cohorts' key to shopper_map.counted_as(event), which counts identities before the cutover day and shoppers from it on.
explanations.weekly-digest: Shopper now keeps its attributes per identity, and ShopperMap links a shopper's identities. Your audience therefore reads one shopper where it read several identities. Penguin's update copies accounts/shoppers.py and messaging/subscriptions.py into your fork: is_subscribed() reads each linked identity's latest consent, so an unsubscribe on any identity holds.

cohort-ltv.reason: ShopperMap.resolve() now links the identities that one login or one verified email ties together. The call returns one shopper where it returned several.

weekly-digest.reason: Shopper now keeps its attributes per identity. The digest's audience reads one linked shopper where it read several identities.

reviews.cohort-ltv: Approved. Counting by the cutover keeps each published day's count, and the kiosk's shoppers stay apart.
reviews.weekly-digest: Approved. The digest writes to each linked shopper once, and an unsubscribe on any of their identities stops it.

shopper-same.explanation: ShopperMap.resolve() now links the identities a login or a shared verified email ties together, one account per device, so it can return a linked shopper's key where it returned an identity's. {title} counts shoppers with only one identity each, so its counts stay the same.
shopper-same.reason: ShopperMap.resolve() returns the linked shopper's key. {title} counts each shopper once either way.

shopper-cutover.explanation: ShopperMap.resolve() now links the identities a login or a shared verified email ties together, one account per device. Your test sees a later login lower a published day's count in {title}. Penguin's update copies accounts/shoppers.py into your fork. Rule count-by-cutover rewrites the count's key to shopper_map.counted_as(event), which counts identities before the cutover day and shoppers from it on.
shopper-cutover.reason: ShopperMap.resolve() now links the identities that one login or one verified email ties together. The call returns one shopper where it returned several.
shopper-cutover.review: Approved. Counting by the cutover keeps each published day's count in {title}.

shopper-consent.explanation: Shopper now keeps its attributes per identity, and ShopperMap links a shopper's identities. {title} therefore reads one shopper where it read several identities. Penguin's update copies accounts/shoppers.py and messaging/subscriptions.py into your fork: is_subscribed() reads each linked identity's latest consent, so an unsubscribe on any identity holds.
shopper-consent.reason: Shopper now keeps its attributes per identity. {title} reads one linked shopper where it read several identities.
shopper-consent.review: Approved. {title} leaves out a shopper who unsubscribed on any of their identities.
